summary: Configured persistent sudo command logging on node1. Every sudo command is recorded in /var/log/sudo-commands.log with timestamp and user information, while sudo syslog output is disabled. The configuration and log data survived a verified node restart.
actions_performed: Created /etc/sudoers.d/90-command-logging with a dedicated logfile and syslog disabled.
Verified live pre- and post-restart sudo command records.
Confirmed test records were absent from /var/log/messages, /var/log/secure, and the systemd journal.
Safely restarted node1 and verified its boot identity changed and logging recovered.

evidence.requirement: Record every sudo command with user and timestamp in /var/log/sudo-commands.log
evidence.summary: sudoers validation passed. Captured records contain timestamps, invoking user 'antrieb', target user 'root', and full commands, including a successful post-restart test.

evidence.requirement: Keep sudo command entries out of the general system log
evidence.summary: Unique pre- and post-restart test commands produced zero matches in messages, secure, and the journal. Persistent configuration contains 'Defaults !syslog'.

Healthy baseline boot ID was 809708f3-1c5f-4e37-ad6a-8bcbae408799. The native reboot command disconnected the transport before its shell acknowledgement printed; its acceptance is recorded in the persistent sudo log. The node became unavailable, recovered with boot ID 5d6afe67-3f7b-4772-82eb-9da68b21bc7b, and retained valid configuration, active rsyslog, prior log data, and correct live logging behavior.
